title: Hawaiian-Style Huli-Huli Pineapple Glaze
description: Pineapple caramelizes at the edges of the skillet before ginger, tomato and coconut aminos turn it into a smooth island-style glaze.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: crushed pineapple in pineapple juice
ingredients.note: Use fruit with its own juice, without added sugar.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

steps.title: Concentrate the pineapple
steps.text: Warm {pn} and {oil} over medium heat for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until the juices become syrupy and the edges begin to color.

steps.title: Simmer the glaze base
steps.text: Add {pi}, {ch}, {gi}, {ga}, {to}, {bs}, {cv} and {a}. Simmer for 4 minutes, scraping up the caramelized pineapple.

steps.title: Smooth the glaze
steps.text: Take off the heat and blend the fruit into the liquid. Return to the pan and bring to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over hot chicken thighs or lean pork. Keep a clean portion warm to add at the table.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 5 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, replace pineapple juice with water, omit the vinegar and halve the ginger. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 66 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 13.7 g total carbohydrate, 1.3 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 120 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 61 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 12.4 g total carbohydrate, 1.3 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 30 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
